name: web/object-3d
title: 3D object
summary: One 3D shape (cube, sphere, ring, gem, star and more) that turns slowly on the page and can be turned with the mouse or a finger.
when: Use when the user wants one 3D object on a page, such as a cube, a sphere, a donut, a gem or a star, that turns slowly and that the viewer can turn with the mouse or a finger.

title.about: The name of the object, shown at the top left of the page and in the browser tab. A few plain words.

shape.about: The shape: one of cube, sphere, cone, cylinder, ring, knot, gem, pyramid, capsule or star. A whole sentence works; the first of these words in it is used.

color.about: The colour of the object: a colour name or a hex code, for example #c0392b.

background.about: The colour of the page behind the object: a colour name or a hex code.

next: Nothing more to do: the page is finished and shows itself in the chat. Do not read it, run it, build it or install anything; tell the user in one or two sentences what the object is. Only when the user asks for a change: edit the lines inside <script id="settings"> in index.html with replace_in_file, for example the line "shape cube", and nothing else.
change: Only when the user asks for a change: replace_in_file(path="{file}", old="shape cube", new="shape gem") changes the shape; the same way for the title, color and background lines inside <script id="settings"> near the top of index.html. Only those four lines are edited.

not_text: Shape not understood, so a cube is shown. Known shapes: cube, sphere, cone, cylinder, ring, knot, gem, pyramid, capsule, star.
Colour not understood, so the default colour is used. Try a colour name or a hex code such as #c0392b.
Background not understood, so the default background is used. Try a colour name or a hex code such as #dff1fb.
